Hedge P&L = carry - FX return (annualised arithmetic means). carry < 0 is the interest-rate cost of selling the currency forward; fx_return < 0 means the franc appreciated, which the hedge earns back. t and p test hedge P&L = 0 (Newey-West).

Carry used for the last month in the sample (Sep 2026, rates of the previous month: CHF -0.04%, USD 3.82%, EUR 2.51%): USD -3.85% per year, EUR -2.55% per year, i.e. 2.12 and 2.09 times the full-sample average carry.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| US equities (S&P 500 TR) | 0.70 [0.48, 0.92] | 0.000 | 0.007 | 16.7% | 16.3% | 15.2% | 14.9% | 321 |
| US Treasuries 10y | 0.83 [0.71, 0.94] | 0.000 | 0.003 | 53.9% | 10.8% | 7.5% | 7.3% | 321 |

| German Bunds 10y | 0.81 [0.69, 0.93] | 0.000 | 0.002 | 36.6% | 7.5% | 6.0% | 5.9% | 321 |
| Foreign 60/40 portfolio | 0.92 [0.72, 1.11] | 0.000 | 0.413 | 26.2% | 11.3% | 9.7% | 9.7% | 321 |

h* = slope of the unhedged franc return on the currency return net of carry. h* < 1: the currency partly hedges the asset by itself; h* > 1: the currency adds to the asset's risk, so hedging more than 100% lowers volatility further. R² = share of the variance removed by hedging at h*.
